blocks.text: Status: Story-established tradition in Weather, consistent with Era Zero Crafted World art.

Origin: Artists transform the inherited human word “weather.” In early Shelter usage it means a system behaving differently without being damaged. Children apply it to unfinished rooms. By Era Zero, Garden Worlds create emotional weather: environments in which relations among color, music, attention, and movement change without a conventional storm.
Era −2: “Bad weather” describes irregular network behavior.
Era −1: Children say an unfinished room has weather. The word becomes the mood of a place before it changes.
Era Zero: Garden Worlds make weather an artistic and relational environment. Visitors notice colors relating differently and music becoming newly perceptible.
Era One: Fewer citizens notice subtle transitions. Gardens simplify; artists shorten performances and make changes more obvious.
Era Two: Some gardens are reduced to a few preserved relation-rules.
Era Three: Local peoples may experience a garden’s remaining pattern as literal weather, even when no air or water is changing.
Present condition: Tradition confirmed; individual surviving gardens unspecified.
Corruption: 2 — later beings may literalize an originally relational artwork.

Visual brief: Begin with a familiar garden but make the “weather” occur between elements: shadows align into chords; flowers do not move, yet their color relationships shift; distant architecture grows easier or harder to notice; pathways become emotionally near or far. Avoid relying only on rain, snow, or fog.
Background traits: Warm-Neutral; Moist; crafted garden biome; contemplative, responsive mood; gentle friction. Animation motif: slow palette relationships and layered music cues.
